title: Where the acts of unbelievers and of believers belong
source_text: XVIII. Ad prius genus pertinent actus infidelium qui videntur honesti & ex virtute profecti. Non enim ex fide promanant, & ex Dei amore, nec etiam ad Dei gloriam referuntur, ut supra jam diximus, ac proinde non possunt inter opera bona & sancta numerari, & talia dici simpliciter. Actiones vero fidelium auxilio Spiritus sancti, & per Christi gratiam factae, ad alterum istud genus referri debent: siquidem non tantum bonae sunt ratione objecti, & quoad substantiam, sed etiam ratione principii & finis, quandoquidem ex charitate fiunt, & tendunt ad Dei gloriam. Ideoque ejusmodi fidelium opera Deo probantur atque accepta sunt, ut vere & proprie bona, & talia simpliciter & absolute loquendo dici debent: licet non omnimodam bonitatem habeant, neque parum a summa perfectione deficiant.
pass_a_gloss: XVIII. To the former kind belong the acts of unbelievers which seem honourable & to proceed from virtue. For they do not flow from faith, & from the love of God, nor are they referred to the glory of God, as we have already said above, & therefore they cannot be numbered among good & holy works, & be called such simply. But the actions of the faithful done by the help of the Holy Spirit, & through the grace of Christ, must be referred to that other kind: since they are good not only by reason of the object, & as to substance, but also by reason of principle & end, inasmuch as they are done from charity, & tend to the glory of God. And therefore such works of the faithful are approved by God & are accepted, as truly & properly good, & ought to be called such simply & absolutely speaking: although they do not have every kind of goodness, & fall not a little short of the highest perfection.
pass_b_english: Thesis XVIII. The acts of unbelievers that look honourable and seem to come from virtue belong to the first kind. As we said above, they do not come from faith and the love of God, and they are not directed to God's glory, so they cannot be counted among good and holy works or simply be called such.

The actions of believers, done with the help of the Holy Spirit and by Christ's grace, belong to the second kind. They are good not only in their object and substance but also in their source and their end, since they are done out of love and aim at God's glory.

That is why such works of believers are approved and accepted by God as truly and properly good, and should be called good simply and without qualification, even though they do not have every kind of goodness and fall well short of the highest perfection.

lemmas.latin: Ad prius genus pertinent actus infidelium
lemmas.gloss: To the former kind belong the acts of unbelievers
by reason of principle and end

choices.why: The scholastic distinction between a defect of kind, which makes an act bad, and a defect of degree, which leaves it good but imperfect.
